Unlike successive bail applica ons under sec on 439 CrPC in changed circumstances, the ling of successive applica ons before the same court, under sec on 438 CrPC, which had been decided the earlier by a speaking order, amounts to recalling of the order, which is barred under sec on 362 CrPC and is legally impermissible.
5. Now the pe oner seeks bail on the ground that as per the prosecu on, the pe oner had failed to recover an amount of Rs.50 lakhs.
However, the said claim was made by the prosecu on without any documentary proof and it based on surmises and conjectures.
In paragraph 6 of the bail pe on, the pe oner submits that his earlier bail was rejected simply because his case was at par with the co-accused whose bail has been dismissed.
In paragraph 7 of the bail pe on, the pe oner seeks bail by saying that it had come in the departmental enquiry that he had served honestly and had not caused any nancial loss.

sentences.text: An order for refusal of bail however, inherently carries certain characteris cs of an interlocutory order in that certain varia on or altera on in the context in which a bail plea is dismissed confers on the detained accused right to le a fresh applica on for bail on certain changed circumstances.
Thus, an order rejec ng prayer for bail does not disempower the Court from considering such plea afresh if there is any altera on of the circumstances.
Condi ons of bail could also be varied if a case is made out for such varia on based on that factor.
Prohibi on contemplated in Sec on 362 of the Code would not apply in such cases.
Hence, we do not think the reasoning on which the impugned order was passed rejec ng the appellant's applica on of bail can be sustained.
The impugned order is set aside and the maHer is remiHed to the High Court.
The bail pe on of the appellant before the High Court shall revive to be examined afresh by the High Court in the light of our observa ons made in this order.

9. In the light of the judicial precedents men oned above and in the given facts and circumstances peculiar to this case, the pe oner fails to jus fy ling of the second applica on for an cipatory bail under sec on 438 CrPC in the same court.
An analysis of above said arguments explicitly point out that the pe oner cannot claim bail by asking this Court to review its own order, which is absolutely impermissible.

10. Any observa on made hereinabove is neither an expression of opinion on the case's merits,
neither the court taking up regular bail nor the trial Court shall advert to these comments.
Pe..on dismissed.

It is claried that in case the pe oner surrenders and les an applica on for bail on or before 29.02.2024, this Court requests the trial Court to expedite hearing of the bail pe on and the State is also directed not to take me for ling response to that pe on.
All pending applica ons, if any, stand disposed.
